newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - West German April CPI down 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - West German April CPI down 0.1 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from economists about west German preliminary April consumer price data, which showed a 0.1 percent month-on-month drop and a 1.4 percent gain year-on-year.

"It's nice and lovely. The data is lower than expected. There is no price pressure and much of the increase at the beginning of the year was seasonal. There is no pipeline inflation pressure. This changes the medium-term outlook as well. It has been proven that all of the increases at the beginning of the year were seasonal and there is no upward pressure. There is no sign at the moment that we have entered an upward trend."

"It is certainly very positive and lower than expected. Falling mineral oil prices and lower package holiday prices contributed to the drop but there is also the fact that companies have very little or no chance to push through cost increases on the consumer level. Unless the dollar goes through the roof, which is not our main scenario, we see no inflation danger in the near-term. It should not change the Bundesbank interest rate outlook. They focus much more on the longer term and they do not want to fuel the dollar. Lower interest rates would not fit into that environment."
